payload.name: Count-event-mentions-with-inflections
payload.description: When a question asks how many times someone performed an activity (won, played, mentioned, etc.), expand keyword searches to cover inflections and singular/plural forms before retrieving memories.
content: For counting questions about past actions, first list morphological variants of the action verb (e.g., win/wins/won/winning) and both singular/plural object nouns (game/games).
Issue keyword searches for each variant and combine with semantic/hybrid search to retrieve memories phrased differently; do not assume a single query captures all mentions.

solves: The agent missed multiple memory entries because it searched only one keyword inflection ("winning games") while the stored memories used different verb forms and singular nouns ("won", "win a game", "game"). The failure mechanism is over-reliance on a single keyword form when counting repeated actions or events. This applies to any count-of-action question where memories may phrase the action with varied inflections or synonyms, so future searches must expand to all morphological variants and combine keyword with semantic retrieval.
